laws.rule: The recreational use of marijuana (Cannabis) is subject to local laws and regulations. It's illegal to transport marijuana (Cannabis) across Canada's international borders (including the United States), even if you are entering or leaving the country. If you break the law, you can receive criminal penalties, including jail time. Make sure you know the local cannabis laws about: legal age possession purchase sharing impairment production Local health authorities have reported illegal drugs may be mixed with more potent substances that can lead to health issues including overdose and death.

laws.rule: To drive in Canada, you may need: an International Driving Permit (IDP) and a valid Australian licence Get an IDP before you leave Australia. items.text: Psilocybin is a restricted drug (Schedule 4) under Canada's Controlled Substances Regulations (SOR/2025-242), in force from 1 October 2026. They replace the 2022 Special Access Program class exemption: section 6 lets a person possess a Schedule 4 Part 1 restricted drug only if, among other listed cases, they obtained it for their own use from a practitioner named in a Health Canada letter of authorization. Otherwise possession stays illegal; no retail or recreational access.
MDMA is also a Schedule 4 restricted drug under SOR/2025-242 (in force 1 October 2026), with the same narrow letter-of-authorization route as psilocybin.
The recreational use of marijuana (Cannabis) is subject to local laws and regulations.
It's illegal to transport marijuana (Cannabis) across Canada's international borders (including the United States), even if you are entering or leaving the country.

Make sure you know the local cannabis laws about: legal age possession purchase sharing impairment production Local health authorities have reported illegal drugs may be mixed with more potent substances that can lead to health issues including overdose and death.
Check the local legal drinking age before buying or drinking alcohol.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A Canadian host can document the guest-speaker or five-day commercial-seminar exemption, a short high-skilled work exemption, or support a CPTPP, entrepreneur or other work-permit route.
baseline_unverified.fastest_entry: CAD $7 eTA for air travel; most approvals arrive within minutes, although supporting-document cases can take several days
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Get the eTA before booking a flight and have the Canadian host classify the activity and prepare its invitation before travel, even when no work permit is required.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: An eTA can remain valid for up to five years or passport expiry and supports repeat short visits, normally up to six months each; the border officer decides the actual admission period.
documents: Australian passport linked to the eTA
Invitation with exact activities and dates
Evidence of the work-permit exemption or permit route
Host contact available for the border officer
steps: Obtain the eTA before booking a flight and verify the linked passport number.
Build one schedule separating meetings, attendance, guest speech, commercial seminar, teaching, performance, remote work, sales and company operation.
Have the Canadian host write the exact IRPR exemption, short-work or permit rationale into the invitation packet.
For CPTPP or entrepreneur work, begin the contract, significant-benefit and permit work well before travel and recheck current processing times.
Carry entry documents, host contacts, payment terms and evidence that foreign business and remote work remain outside the Canadian labour market.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: In national parks: never feed, approach or follow wildlife. Keep at least 30 m from deer, elk, moose and sheep, and 100 m from bears, wolves, coyotes and cougars. Leave rocks, fossils, antlers and plants where they are.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Look at and record Indigenous and other cultural sites, but leave artefacts, bones and remains exactly as found. Removing or defacing cultural artefacts is illegal.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Parks Canada; the Indigenous Nations whose lands the parks are on.
